senses.gloss: The way a character or story develops from start to finish.
examples: The show gives the villain a full redemption *arc*.
Her character *arc* takes up the whole second season.
The novel's emotional *arc* builds slowly toward the last chapter.

senses.gloss: A flash of electricity that jumps across a gap.
examples: A blue *arc* jumped between the two terminals.
The welder struck an *arc* against the steel plate.
Loose wiring can throw *arcs* that start a fire.

senses.gloss: The curved underside of the foot between the heel and the toes.
examples: These insoles support the *arch* of your foot.
He has high *arches*, so most sneakers hurt.
Flat feet mean the *arch* has collapsed.

senses.gloss: A single compressed file that holds a group of other files.
examples: Download the *archive* and unzip it into this folder.
The whole project fits in one 40-megabyte *archive*.
She emailed me a password-protected *archive*.

senses.gloss: An area of public activity where people compete or argue.
examples: She entered the political *arena* at twenty-six.
Two startups are fighting it out in the same *arena*.
The courtroom became the *arena* for their long feud.

senses.gloss: Weapons, especially guns, spoken of as a group.
examples: The Constitution mentions the right to bear *arms*.
Both countries agreed to limit nuclear *arms*.
The rebels laid down their *arms* at dawn.

senses.gloss: A branch or division of a larger organization.
examples: Research is the fastest-growing *arm* of the company.
The charity's legal *arm* handles evictions.
Congress created the agency as an investigative *arm*.

senses.gloss: The side part of a chair or sofa that supports your arm.
examples: He gripped the *arms* of the chair and stood up.
The cat sleeps on the *arm* of the couch.
One *arm* of the recliner is coming loose.

senses.gloss: A large and varied group of things offered or faced at once.
examples: The store carries a dazzling *array* of hot sauces.
She faced an *array* of federal charges.
A whole *array* of tests came back normal.

senses.gloss: A sudden stop in the working of something, especially the heart.
examples: He went into cardiac *arrest* on the flight.
The drug caused a temporary *arrest* of the tumor's growth.
Paramedics treated her for respiratory *arrest*.

senses.gloss: A person or thing that has just come to a place.
examples: The shelter takes in new *arrivals* every night.
She's a recent *arrival* from Chicago.
The store puts new *arrivals* in the front window.

senses.gloss: The whole set of skills or resources someone can draw on.
examples: A changeup is the best pitch in his *arsenal*.
Patience is the strongest tool in a teacher's *arsenal*.
The lawyer had an *arsenal* of precedents ready.

senses.gloss: A main road or route that carries heavy traffic.
examples: I-95 is the East Coast's main *artery*.
Snow shut down every *artery* into the city.
The bridge is a vital *artery* for freight.

senses.gloss: A single object, especially one of a set.
examples: Every *article* of clothing was folded in tissue paper.
Customs asks you to declare *articles* worth over 800 dollars.
Not one *article* in the case was worth stealing.

senses.gloss: One of the words a, an, or the, used in front of a noun.
examples: Russian has no *articles*, so English ones take practice.
Use the definite *article* when both speakers know which one you mean.
He dropped every *article* from his notes to save space.

senses.gloss: A separately numbered section of a treaty, contract, or constitution.
examples: *Article* II lays out the president's powers.
The union cited *Article* 12 of the contract.
Both sides broke several *articles* of the treaty.

senses.gloss: A professional performer, especially a singer or musician.
examples: The label signed three new *artists* this year.
She's my favorite *artist* on the whole playlist.
Local *artists* play the bar every Friday.

senses.gloss: The drawings, photos, and layout prepared for a book, album, or ad.
examples: The band approved the album *artwork* last week.
Send the *artwork* to the printer by Friday.
The cover *artwork* was done by a local illustrator.

senses.gloss: A rise to a higher rank, position, or level of success.
examples: His *ascent* from the mailroom to vice president took nine years.
The book traces the party's *ascent* after the war.
Her *ascent* in the polls surprised everyone.

senses.gloss: A hardwood tree with tough pale timber, or the wood itself.
examples: A row of *ash* trees lines the driveway.
Baseball bats used to be turned from *ash*.
A beetle has killed millions of *ash* trees in the Midwest.

senses.gloss: A remark that steps away from the main subject.
examples: As an *aside*, the coffee in that building is terrible.
He added a short *aside* about his childhood.
Her lecture was full of funny *asides*.

senses.gloss: A person or quality that is genuinely useful to a group.
examples: Her calm is a real *asset* in an emergency.
He's been an *asset* to the department since day one.
Patience is the greatest *asset* a coach can have.

senses.gloss: An older name for a hospital for people with mental illness.
examples: The building was a state *asylum* until 1974.
In the novel she is locked away in an *asylum*.
Most of the old *asylums* were torn down.

senses.gloss: One of the two upper chambers of the heart.
examples: Blood enters the right *atrium* from the veins.
The scan showed a small hole between the *atria*.
The left *atrium* pushes blood into the ventricle.

senses.gloss: A sudden short period of an illness or strong feeling.
examples: He had a heart *attack* while shoveling snow.
Cold air can trigger an asthma *attack*.
She gets panic *attacks* in crowded stores.

senses.gloss: Strong public criticism of a person or an idea.
examples: The senator launched a bitter *attack* on the press.
The column was a direct *attack* on the mayor's record.
He's used to *attacks* from both parties.

senses.gloss: A careful official review of something other than accounts.
examples: The city ordered a safety *audit* of every bridge.
We ran an energy *audit* on the house before winter.
The *audit* found a dozen broken links on the site.

senses.gloss: A possible way of doing something or making progress.
examples: We've explored every *avenue* and come up empty.
Selling online opened a new *avenue* for the shop.
Appealing the ruling is her only remaining *avenue*.

senses.gloss: Sunglasses with thin metal frames and large teardrop lenses.
examples: He wore mirrored *aviators* the whole flight.
She pushed her *aviators* up onto her head.
A pair of gold *aviators* sat on the dashboard.

senses.gloss: A sum of money granted to someone by a court or official body.
examples: The jury's *award* came to two million dollars.
The judge cut the *award* in half on appeal.
She won a research *award* of fifty thousand dollars.

senses.gloss: Sudden dismissal from a job, or the cancellation of a program.
examples: Two hundred workers got the *ax* in March.
The show faced the *ax* after one season.
Nobody knew who would be next for the *ax*.

senses.gloss: Sudden dismissal from a job, or the cancellation of a program.
examples: The network gave the sitcom the *axe*.
Half the department got the *axe* last quarter.
His pet project was first in line for the *axe*.

senses.gloss: A confused noise of many people talking at once.
examples: A *babble* of voices filled the hallway.
I couldn't hear the announcement over the *babble*.
The room went from a *babble* to total silence.

senses.gloss: An affectionate name for a partner or someone you love.
examples: Good night, *baby*.
He calls her *baby* in front of everyone.
*Baby*, I'm home!

senses.gloss: A project someone created and cares about as their own.
examples: The community garden is her *baby*.
Don't touch the database, that's his *baby*.
The festival started as a side project and became my *baby*.

senses.gloss: The part of something that is farthest from the front.
examples: The recipe is printed on the *back* of the box.
We sat in the *back* of the classroom.
There's a small yard at the *back* of the house.

senses.gloss: Extra people or equipment ready to help if they are needed.
examples: The officer called for *backup* before going in.
We keep a generator as *backup*.
Two more ambulances arrived as *backup*.

senses.gloss: A build-up of traffic, water, or waste caused by a blockage.
examples: There's a five-mile *backup* on the interstate.
A sewer *backup* flooded the basement.
Snow caused *backups* at every intersection.

senses.gloss: A sign or mark that shows a quality or an achievement.
examples: He wears the nickname as a *badge* of honor.
Calluses were a *badge* of hard work.
For them the scar is a *badge* of survival.

senses.gloss: Painful past experiences that still affect how someone behaves.
examples: He brings a lot of emotional *baggage* to the relationship.
Every candidate carries some political *baggage*.
She left the marriage with plenty of *baggage*.

senses.gloss: Something offered to tempt a person into a trap or a reaction.
examples: The low price was just *bait* to get you into the store.
Don't take the *bait* when he insults you.
Police left an unlocked car as *bait*.

senses.gloss: A steady position in which you do not fall over.
examples: She lost her *balance* on the icy step.
Yoga has improved my *balance*.
He held both arms out for *balance*.

senses.gloss: A state in which different things are present in the right amounts.
examples: Finding a work-life *balance* took him years.
The sauce has a nice *balance* of sweet and sour.
The court has to strike a *balance* between safety and privacy.

senses.gloss: The upper floor of seats in a theater or movie house.
examples: Our tickets were in the second row of the *balcony*.
The *balcony* was closed for the matinee.
Kids used to sneak up to the *balcony*.

senses.gloss: A round object that is thrown, kicked, or hit in games.
examples: The dog brought the *ball* back every time.
He hit the *ball* over the fence.
We lost three *balls* in the tall grass.

senses.gloss: Something squeezed or rolled into a round mass.
examples: Roll the dough into a *ball* and let it rest.
The cat unwound a whole *ball* of yarn.
He crushed the letter into a *ball*.

senses.gloss: Heavy material carried in a ship or balloon to keep it steady.
examples: The tanker took on seawater as *ballast*.
They dumped *ballast* to gain altitude.
Without *ballast* the boat rides too high.

senses.gloss: A large bag of hot air with a basket that carries people.
examples: We went up in a hot-air *balloon* at sunrise.
Dozens of *balloons* rose over the valley.
The *balloon* landed in a soybean field.

senses.gloss: A wide advertisement across the top of a web page.
examples: Ad blockers strip out most *banners*.
The site's *banner* follows you as you scroll.
We paid for a *banner* on the homepage.

senses.gloss: A sharp, unkind remark.
examples: She got in one last *barb* before leaving.
His speech was full of *barbs* aimed at the coach.
The compliment carried a *barb*.

senses.gloss: An agreement in which each side promises to do something.
examples: We made a *bargain*: he cooks, I clean.
You've kept your end of the *bargain*.
The defendant took a plea *bargain*.

senses.gloss: The short, loud sound a dog makes.
examples: One sharp *bark* woke the whole house.
The *barks* got louder as I came up the walk.
Her dog has a deep *bark* for such a small animal.

senses.gloss: The long metal tube of a gun that the bullet travels through.
examples: He looked straight down the *barrel* of the rifle.
The *barrel* was still warm.
Both *barrels* of the shotgun were empty.

senses.gloss: A standard unit for measuring oil, equal to 42 gallons.
examples: Crude oil closed at 78 dollars a *barrel*.
The field produces thirty thousand *barrels* a day.
A cold snap pushed the price per *barrel* higher.

senses.gloss: Something that keeps people apart or stops progress.
examples: Language was the biggest *barrier* at her new job.
Cost is still a *barrier* to treatment.
The law removed several *barriers* for small businesses.

senses.gloss: A wide round bowl used for holding water.
examples: She filled a *basin* with warm water.
The nurse set a *basin* beside the bed.
He rinsed the brushes in a shallow *basin*.

senses.gloss: The spooning of juices or fat over meat while it roasts.
examples: Frequent *basting* keeps the turkey from drying out.
The *basting* liquid was butter, wine, and herbs.
Give it one more *basting* before it comes out.

senses.gloss: A wooden or metal club used to hit the ball in baseball.
examples: He swung the *bat* and missed.
The kid picked out an aluminum *bat*.
Both *bats* were still in the trunk of the car.

senses.gloss: A group of things or people dealt with at the same time.
examples: The office processes a *batch* of applications every Monday.
A new *batch* of recruits arrived at the base.
We sent the letters out in three *batches*.

senses.gloss: A bathroom, in the way homes are counted and described.
examples: The apartment has two bedrooms and one *bath*.
The listing says three beds and two *baths*.
They added a full *bath* upstairs.

senses.gloss: The short stick runners hand to each other in a relay race.
examples: She dropped the *baton* on the second handoff.
He passed the *baton* and collapsed on the grass.
The *baton* has to change hands inside the zone.

senses.gloss: A heavy stick carried by police officers as a weapon.
examples: Officers were issued helmets and *batons*.
He banged on the door with his *baton*.
The department is reviewing its rules on *baton* use.

senses.gloss: The player whose turn it is to hit the ball in baseball.
examples: The *batter* fouled off six pitches in a row.
He struck out the first three *batters*.
The *batter* stepped out of the box.

senses.gloss: The crime of hitting or violently touching another person.
examples: He was charged with assault and *battery*.
The *battery* charge was dropped before trial.
She sued him for *battery* after the fight.

senses.gloss: A long series of similar things, especially tests or questions.
examples: The doctor ordered a *battery* of tests.
Recruits face a *battery* of physical exams.
He survived a *battery* of questions from reporters.
